verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents programmatic lifecycle control at the cluster and Node Pool level: the CKS API can create, list, update, and delete clusters, and Terraform can manage infrastructure as code. Node Pools can be scaled to demand with the Cluster Autoscaler, and On-Demand and Spot capacity is sold pay-as-you-go without long-term commitments. However, nothing documents stop, start, or restart of individual instances (bare-metal Nodes inside Node Pools), and billing is not explicitly tied to running time. Missing for 10: per-instance start/stop/restart API, documented stopped-state or per-running-time billing semantics, Node Pool resize via API (only the autoscaler is documented), independent hands-on corroboration.
